title: RBAC: add explicit permissions for Audit Logs API + export actions
author: Jordan Lee
body: Summary: This PR introduces explicit RBAC permissions for the new Audit Logs API surface (list/filter/get/export) and updates default roles + migration notes accordingly. Motivation: Today audit log access is effectively implied by broad admin privileges in a few places; for enterprise audits we need a stable, reviewable permission boundary for (1) viewing audit events, (2) exporting audit events to external sinks (S3/webhook/SIEM), and (3) managing audit log configuration (retention/export destinations). This also unblocks Console backend work (ENG-2493) to enforce RBAC in a consistent way. Details: Adds new permissions: audit_logs.read (List/get audit events via Console/API), audit_logs.export (Create exports / generate export tokens / trigger export jobs), audit_logs.export.manage (Create/update/delete export sinks, credentials references, and destination configuration), audit_logs.retention.manage (Set retention and redaction configuration; Private deployments may scope this differently), audit_logs.access_token.issue (Issue short-lived export/download tokens for UI + API). Updates default roles: Org Admin: includes audit_logs.read + audit_logs.export by default (keeps current admin behavior for most customers); Security Admin (if enabled): includes audit_logs.read, audit_logs.export, audit_logs.export.manage, audit_logs.retention.manage; Read-only Admin: includes audit_logs.read only (no export). Keeps Audit Logs gated behind existing admin-only feature flags on the application side; this PR only establishes the canonical permission names and role bindings in the policy bundle. Backwards compatibility: For environments where Audit Logs API is already live behind a flag, access will remain functionally unchanged for Org Admin users (new permissions are included). For custom roles that previously relied on coarse permissions (e.g., console.admin), migration guidance is included below. Migration notes (for release notes / rollout): 1) If you have custom roles that should access Audit Logs, grant audit_logs.read. 2) If you have custom roles that should export audit logs, grant audit_logs.export and (optionally) audit_logs.export.manage depending on whether they should manage sinks vs only trigger exports. 3) Managing retention/redaction requires audit_logs.retention.manage. 4) For Private, cluster operators may need audit_logs.retention.manage at the platform scope; follow-up PRs will refine scoping as Private control plane permissions land. Testing: Policy compilation tests updated; added snapshots to ensure default role bindings include the new permissions. Notes for reviewers: Permission naming follows the namespace decision from architecture thread (audit_logs.*) to avoid mixing with api.* / console.*; see linked docs update in this PR. Future work: Enforce these permissions in Console backend endpoints (ENG-2493) and in exporter management endpoints once the exporter config API lands.
commits: rbac: add audit_logs.* permissions to permission catalog
rbac: bind audit_logs permissions into default roles (org_admin, security_admin, read_only_admin)
docs: add migration notes for audit logs permissions + examples for custom roles
tests: update policy compilation snapshots for default roles
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng): Can we separate 'export' from 'manage export sinks'? We don’t want every admin who can download logs to also be able to point exports at a new endpoint. Also, please confirm that read-only admin doesn’t get export.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep — split into audit_logs.export (trigger export / download) vs audit_logs.export.manage (create/update/delete sinks). Read-only admin gets audit_logs.read only. Pushed commit 7f1c2a0 with the split + updated docs.

Chloe Martin (Console backend): For export token issuance, is that covered by audit_logs.export or should it be separate? We need to issue short-lived tokens for UI downloads without giving sink management.

Jordan Lee (author): Added audit_logs.access_token.issue so Console can gate token issuance separately if needed. Default roles include it alongside audit_logs.export; but custom roles can choose tighter control. See migration doc update.
Ethan Park (Identity/Control plane): Naming looks good. One concern: retention/redaction config might be product-tiered; can we keep that as a separate permission so we can entitle it later?
Jordan Lee (author): Agreed — added audit_logs.retention.manage separate from export/manage. Default Security Admin includes it; Org Admin does not (to reduce accidental changes).

Olga Petrov (GRC): Please ensure the migration notes include a clear statement auditors can understand: who can view, who can export, who can change retention. Also add a short note that access changes are themselves audited elsewhere.
Jordan Lee (author): Added a short 'Auditor-friendly summary' section to the migration doc. Re: auditing access changes — noted as covered by RBAC change audit events in ENG-2484 (separate repo).
release_notes: RBAC: Introduce explicit audit_logs.* permissions and update default roles to support Audit Logs API access and exports. Custom roles may need updates; see migration doc.
